question: The typically Judo platform is of which shape?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Square**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The standard competition platform used in **Judo** is a **square-shaped mat**, commonly referred to as the **tatami**.
 
• The **contest area** is typically **10 meters x 10 meters**, with an additional **3-meter safety area** surrounding it to ensure the safety of participants.
 
• The square layout ensures **equal opportunities** for both players, providing enough space for techniques like **throws, grappling, and groundwork**.
 
• The mats are made of **shock-absorbing materials** to minimize injuries during high-impact throws and falls.
 
• The **International Judo Federation (IJF)** regulations mandate the use of a square contest area to standardize competitions globally, including major events like the **Olympics** and **World Championships**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Judo History:**

 
 
• **Judo** was founded in **1882** by **Jigoro Kano** in Japan.
 
• It emphasizes **leverage, technique, and balance** rather than brute strength.
 
• Judo became an **Olympic sport in 1964** during the Tokyo Games.
 
 
 
• **Tatami Mats:**
 
 
• The mats used in Judo are known as **tatami**.
 
• Traditionally, they were made from **rice straw**, but modern versions use materials like **foam**.
 
• The tatami provides a **non-slip surface** and cushions falls to prevent injuries.
 
 
 
• **Other Shapes in Combat Sports:**
 
 
• **Rectangular:** Used in sports like **wrestling** and **boxing**, suitable for movement patterns in those sports.
 
• **Hexagonal:** Seen in **mixed martial arts (MMA)** to enhance visibility and mobility.
 
• **Circular:** Common in traditional martial arts or **sumo wrestling** to emphasize boundaries.
 
 
 
• **Safety Regulations:**
 
 
• The **International Judo Federation (IJF)** mandates a **3-meter safety area** around the contest area to prevent injuries during high-intensity matches.
 
• The **shock-absorbing mats** are maintained to ensure safe competition conditions.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Judo Belt System:**

 
 
• Judokas progress through a **belt ranking system** (kyu and dan grades) based on their skill levels.
 
• The belt colors range from **white (beginner)** to **black (expert)**.
 
 
 
• **Scoring in Judo:**
 
 
• Points are awarded for techniques like **throws (ippon), pins (osaekomi), and submissions**.
 
• An **ippon** signifies a perfect throw or submission, instantly ending the match.
